title: Hollow by TxPipe: Headless dApp Framework, a friendly SDK for off-chain development

ms.promise:
- Publicly available source code for the Hollow Framework
- Publicly available usage documentation for the Hollow Framework
- A public Rust crate released in crates.io
- A mock runtime component to test Hollow applications built with the framework
ms.criteria: A developer is able to build a basic Hollow application that interacts with a mock Cardano network by following the available documentation.
ms.report:
NOTE: due to naming conflicts with other libraries and projects, we had to rename ours from “Hollow” to “Balius”. Nothing in the scope has changed, just the name. Previous links mentioning Hollow are redirected to their corresponding content under the Balius name.
In the following Github repository you will find the complete source code for the framework component of the project:
https://github.com/txpipe/balius 
In the following site you will find public documentation with install and usage instructions for the Balius (ex Hollow) Framework:
https://balius.txpipe.io 
In the following link you will find a publicly available Rust crate that developers can use to add the framework as dependency on their Rust projects:
https://crates.io/crates/balius 
In the following link you will a video describing the deliverables of the milestones and a quick example of how to code and compile a basic app using the framework:
https://youtu.be/z_34DrO9MGU

The Balius runtime has been successfully integrated into Demeter as a managed service, enabling developers to deploy and operate headless dApps with minimal overhead. Since its release, it has seen early adoption within the Cardano developer community and has been actively used by the TxPipe team for testing and validation during its development.
 Key usage metrics:
・Total number of Demeter projects with Balius workers = 16
・Total number of Balius workers deployed in Demeter = 36
